_comment: EXPANSION allowlist -- a staged local experiment, not a production source list.
config/sources-allowlist.json (production) and sources-allowlist.pilot.json are
untouched by this file.
BASIS FOR COLLECTION, per platform, read on 2026-09-02 and unchanged since:
Greenhouse (docs.greenhouse.io/job-board.html): "Job Board data is publicly
available, so authentication is not required for any GET endpoints." Documents no
rate limit, no caching policy, no attribution requirement and no redistribution
terms. Silence leaves the question open; it does not answer it in our favour.
Lever (github.com/lever/postings-api): GET is public and unauthenticated. "All job
postings in the published state are publicly viewable. These jobs may be scraped by
third parties." An acknowledgement of what happens, not a grant of rights.
That basis is PER PLATFORM and therefore identical for every board below. What is
per-board is only whether the board is live, which the collection run itself records
in each manifest -- probing every board separately first would double the traffic to
the same hosts to learn what one run already tells us.
PUBLIC DISPLAY / REDISTRIBUTION: NOT ESTABLISHED for any board here, and neither
vendor could grant it -- the postings are the EMPLOYERS' content. This is a private
local pilot against an isolated test database. Nothing here is cleared to go in front
of users, and nothing in this file should be read as saying otherwise.
NOT CHECKED: no individual employer's terms were read; no permission was sought.
robots.txt is re-fetched before every board request and refusal aborts that board.
